import "date"
import "regexp"
// This target's incidents (any probe of its base name), and the ones about
// everything: this host's Wi-Fi, the line, upstream.
base = regexp.replaceAllString(r: /(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)$/, v: "${target}", t: "")
re = regexp.compile(v: "(^|,)(?i)" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: base) + "(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)?(,|$)")
from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: date.sub(d: 7d, from: v.timeRangeStart), stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "loss_incident" and (r._field == "class" or r._field == "confidence" or r._field == "summary" or r._field == "end_epoch" or r._field == "targets" or r._field == "minutes"))
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.class == "local_wifi" or r.class == "local_link" or r.class == "upstream" or regexp.matchRegexpString(r: re, v: r.targets))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.class != "probe_miss" and r.end_epoch * 1000000000 >= int(v: v.timeRangeStart))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, timeEnd: time(v: r.end_epoch * 1000000000), text: "Loss incident, " + r.class + " (" + r.confidence + " confidence, " + string(v: r.minutes) + " min): " + r.summary, tags: "incident," + r.class}))

import "regexp"
// pathmeter stores one path per base name (docs/path.md): match that name, any case.
base = regexp.replaceAllString(r: /(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)$/, v: "${target}", t: "")
re = regexp.compile(v: "^(?i)" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: base) + "$")
from(bucket: "smokeping") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "path_trace" and r.target =~ re and
      (r._field == "changed" or r._field == "as_changed" or r._field == "as_path"))
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.changed or r.as_changed)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, text: (if r.as_changed then "AS path changed (experimental): now " + r.as_path else "Path changed (experimental), same AS path " + r.as_path), tags: "experimental"}))

title: Target Detail – every layer for one target
description: Pick a target and see everything measured for it: ICMP, the TCP handshake, HTTP/1.1, /2 and /3, and DNS when the target is a resolver. Targets pair by name across probes (Google, Google_h2, Google_tcp443; W_<service>_icmp, _tcp, _h1–_h3 for the DNS wizard). A layer the target has no probe for says "not measured".

import "strings"
import "influxdata/influxdb/schema"
schema.tagValues(bucket: "smokeping", tag: "target", start: -24h, predicate: (r) => r._measurement == "latency" or r._measurement == "tcp_latency" or r._measurement == "http_latency" or r._measurement == "dns_latency") |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _value: regexp.replaceAllString(r: /(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)$/, v: r._value, t: "") })) |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with key: strings.toLower(v: r._value) })) |> group(columns: ["key"]) |> sort(columns: ["_value"]) |> first() |> group() |> keep(columns: ["_value"]) |> sort()
list.description: Targets with a point in the last 24 hours (SmokePing's step is 5 minutes). A link can still bring a name that is not listed: the first row then says when that target was last measured and, for a retired Netflix appliance name, which slot measures the appliances now.

panels.title: ${target} – what is measured, over the selected range
Time since the last measurement
panels.description: How long ago any probe of this target (ICMP, TCP, HTTP or DNS) last wrote a point inside the selected range, and when that point is. Relative to now: green within 11 minutes (two steps at the default 5-minute step), orange within a day, red beyond. Red means the tiles beside it describe the past, not the present; a range that ends in the past is always red. "no data in this range": nothing from this target in the range at all.

panels.title: Is it measured now?
panels.description: Whether this target wrote a point in the last 24 hours, whatever the selected range. When it did not: when it stopped, and, for a retired Netflix appliance name, which slot (Netflix_<slot>_<site>) measures the appliances now: the slots keep their names while the appliance behind each changes daily (target_host records which). The newest point is looked for in the range and the 30 days before it. Click the text to open the slot, or the Netflix side-by-side.

targets.query:
import "array"
import "date"
import "regexp"
import "strings"
// Any name a link brings (Google, Google_h2, cloudflare) selects the whole target:
// drop the probe suffix, then match every probe of that base name, any case.
base = regexp.replaceAllString(r: /(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)$/, v: "${target}", t: "")
re = regexp.compile(v: "^(?i)" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: base) + "(_h[123]|_tcp(443)?|_icmp)?$")
// The newest point of this target up to now (not the range's end: a past range
// must not read as "stopped"), reaching 30 days back from the range start so a
// target that stopped before the range still says when.
newest = from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start: date.sub(d: 30d, from: v.timeRangeStart), stop: now())
  |> filter(fn:(r)=> (r._measurement == "latency" or r._measurement == "tcp_latency" or r._measurement == "http_latency" or r._measurement == "dns_latency") and r.target =~ re and r._field == "loss")
  |> last() |> keep(columns:["_time","category"]) |> group() |> sort(columns:["_time"], desc:true) |> limit(n:1)
  |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
// The Netflix slots keep their names while the appliance behind each changes daily
// (target_host records which). A retired appliance name ends in its slot number:
// the live slot carrying that number is where its measurements continue.
slot = regexp.findString(r: /_[0-9]+$/, v: base)
slotRe = regexp.compile(v: if slot == "" then "^$" else "^[A-Za-z]+" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: slot) + "_")
live = from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:-24h)
  |> filter(fn:(r)=> r._measurement == "latency" and r.category == "netflix" and r._field == "loss" and r.target =~ slotRe)
  |> last() |> keep(columns:["target"]) |> group() |> limit(n:1)
  |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
since = from(bucket:"smokeping") |> range(start:-1y)
  |> filter(fn:(r)=> r._measurement == "target_host" and r._field == "host" and r.category == "netflix" and r.target =~ slotRe)
  |> first() |> keep(columns:["_time","target"]) |> group() |> sort(columns:["_time"]) |> limit(n:1)
  |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
when = if exists newest._time then strings.replace(v: strings.substring(v: string(v: newest._time), start: 0, end: 16), t: "T", u: " ", i: 1) + " UTC" else ""
category = if exists newest.category then newest.category else ""
slotName = if exists live.target and exists since._time and category == "netflix" then live.target else ""
sinceDay = if exists since._time then strings.substring(v: string(v: since._time), start: 0, end: 10) else ""
stale = not exists newest._time or int(v: now()) - int(v: newest._time) >= 86400000000000
array.from(rows: [{
  _time: now(),
  // The data link opens the slot; for a target without one it opens this target again.
  slot: if slotName != "" then slotName else base,
  _value: if not exists newest._time then "no data: nothing from this target in the range nor in the 30 days before it"
    else if not stale then "measured in the last 24 h: newest point " + when
    else if slotName != "" then "stopped " + when + " · retired name: its slot is measured as " + slotName + " since " + sinceDay
    else if category == "netflix" then "stopped " + when + " · retired name: the Netflix appliances are measured as the Netflix_<slot>_<site> targets"
    else "stopped " + when + " · nothing measured since (removed from the targets, or its probe stopped)"}])
  |> keep(columns:["_time","_value","slot"])

panels.title: Monitor deaf in range
panels.description: Minutes inside the range in which this Pi's own radio heard nothing: Wi-Fi samples in which the uplink's received-packet counter did not move, or the radio was not associated (the definition the alerter, the doctor and the inference module use). Each deaf sample counts the time since the one before it, 10 s by default. Loss in those minutes is the monitor's, not any destination's: subtract it before reading the loss tiles. "none": no deaf sample in the range, or no Wi-Fi uplink (a wired Pi). The "Monitor deaf" and "Loss incidents" annotations mark the spans on the charts; a Monitor deaf span can be longer than these minutes, since the inference period around a short hang covers the clean bins beside it. It reads every Wi-Fi sample in the range (8 640 a day at the default 10 s), so a range of months takes a while to load.

panels.title: Service
panels.description: What this target measures. Value: its service name (docs/taxonomy.md), the label config-manager resolves from the rules, or the override set for this install; the small text over it: its service categories. Not the probe bucket (topsites, netflix...). "unknown (no rule yet)": no rule says yet, not a broken target; the name is then the target's title. As the exporter last recorded it; "no label yet": it has not written one (ClickHouse mode, or the first minutes after an upgrade). Who delivers it is the next tile. The stat reduces over every field (/.*/) on purpose: the string frame is named by its _field label, so a pattern on _value or Value matches nothing and the tile shows its noValue text.

panels.title: Delivered by
panels.description: Who delivers this target: the network its host answers from (its origin AS, from the routing table on the Pi; docs/taxonomy.md, Delivery). Value: that network's operator; the small text over it: its kind (CDN, content network, embedded cache, cloud origin, access network, transit, DNS infrastructure, academic network, local network, other network). "network not identified": no IPv4 answer or no AS lookup yet, not an error; "not looked up yet": a label written before the delivery axis existed. As the exporter last recorded it; "no label yet": it has not written one. Reduces over every field (/.*/), as the Service tile.

panels.title: ICMP
panels.description: Ping (FPing): the network path, no application. "not measured": this target has no such probe (or it wrote nothing in the range). The loss is the mean over the range, this monitor's deaf minutes included: see "Monitor deaf in range".

panels.title: TCP handshake
panels.description: SYN / SYN-ACK to port 443: the transport floor under HTTP. "not measured": this target has no such probe (or it wrote nothing in the range). The loss is the mean over the range, this monitor's deaf minutes included: see "Monitor deaf in range".

panels.title: HTTP
panels.description: A HEAD request over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (connect + TLS + request + response headers, minus DNS). "not measured": this target has no such probe (or it wrote nothing in the range). The loss is the mean over the range, this monitor's deaf minutes included: see "Monitor deaf in range".

panels.title: DNS
panels.description: A DNS query answered by this target, when it is a resolver. "not measured": this target has no such probe (or it wrote nothing in the range). The loss is the mean over the range, this monitor's deaf minutes included: see "Monitor deaf in range".

panels.title: ICMP – ${target} – latency (ms)
panels.description: Ping (FPing): the network path, no application. Line: median; shade: 10th–90th percentile; both of every ping in each point's window (one 5-minute cycle on a short range, many on a long one).

panels.title: ICMP – ${target} – loss (%)
panels.description: Share of the cycle's probes that got no answer.

panels.title: TCP handshake – ${target} – latency (ms)
panels.description: SYN / SYN-ACK to port 443: the transport floor under HTTP. Line: median; shade: 10th–90th percentile; both of every ping in each point's window (one 5-minute cycle on a short range, many on a long one).

panels.title: TCP handshake – ${target} – loss (%)
panels.description: Share of the cycle's probes that got no answer.

panels.title: HTTP – ${target} – fetch time by version, median (ms)
panels.description: A HEAD request over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (connect + TLS + request + response headers, minus DNS). One line per version; a downgraded fetch counts as a failure, not as the lower version. Each line is the median of every fetch of that version in the point's window.

panels.title: HTTP – ${target} – failed fetches (%)
panels.description: Fetches that failed or did not use the version they were asked to.

panels.title: DNS – ${target} – latency (ms)
panels.description: A DNS query answered by this target, when it is a resolver. Line: median; shade: 10th–90th percentile; both of every ping in each point's window (one 5-minute cycle on a short range, many on a long one).

defaults.noValue: no DNS data for this target in this range: resolvers are targets of their own (for example GoogleDNS)

panels.title: DNS – ${target} – loss (%)
panels.description: Share of the cycle's probes that got no answer.

defaults.noValue: no DNS data for this target in this range: resolvers are targets of their own (for example GoogleDNS)

panels.title: Path – ${target} – last trace in range (experimental)
panels.description: EXPERIMENTAL. A Paris traceroute (ICMP) once an hour from the path meter. A router's reply time is its slow path's and rate-limited: read it as a description, not as that hop's latency. A change is counted after two traces in a row show it. See docs/path.md. Hops that did not answer are left out of the table; a private hop has no AS. AS from CAIDA's RouteViews prefix-to-AS table; a router on an exchange point's LAN (not announced) is named by its exchange, from PeeringDB. The name (PTR) is the reverse DNS name the operator gave the address: often a hint of where the router is, sometimes stale; it never counts toward a path change. Each row takes its AS's color, so a run of hops in one network reads as one block; the color comes from the AS number (modulo 12), so an AS keeps it on every target, and two networks can share one. Gray: a private, CGNAT, IPv4 loopback, link-local or ULA address, or a hop with no AS (an exchange port without one included).

defaults.noValue: No path: the path meter is off (smoking-pi enable pathmeter), or it has not traced this target in the selected range.

panels.title: Path changes – ${target} (experimental)
panels.description: Times in the selected range when the path changed: its AS path, its hops, or the address the name resolved to. EXPERIMENTAL. A Paris traceroute (ICMP) once an hour from the path meter. A router's reply time is its slow path's and rate-limited: read it as a description, not as that hop's latency. A change is counted after two traces in a row show it. See docs/path.md.
